articles.title: Empresas brasileiras que adotaram IA enfrentam desafio de encontrar profissionais preparados para usar a tecnologia, diz estudo | G1
articles.standfirst: De cada 100 empresas pesquisadas, 25 disseram que essa falta de capacitação é um problema.
articles.summary: De cada 100 empresas pesquisadas, 25 disseram que essa falta de capacitação é um problema.
articles.body:
Um estudo da Fundação Getúlio Vargas constatou que quase metade das empresas brasileiras já adotou a inteligência artificial. Elas, agora, enfrentam um desafio: encontrar profissionais preparados para usar as novas tecnologias.

Uma inteligência artificial turbinada, programada com matemática complexa e algoritmos super sofisticados. Para monitorar - a 200 km dali, e a 7 mil metros de profundidade - centenas de poços do pré-sal.

“Existe um simulador daquele poço que leva em consideração todos os equipamentos que estão ali presentes. Junto com a IA, nós conseguimos identificar um problema em uma válvula e esse problema na válvula, uma vez que ele foi sanado, a gente conseguiu restaurar a produção daquele poço e evitar meses de perda de produção que seriam feitos sem usar essa tecnologia”, diz João Vitor Bernardino, diretor de operações da Wise.

E não é só para quem lida com tecnologia de ponta. A Fundação Getúlio Vargas fez um estudo com 3 mil empresas. Em 2025, 28,7% delas usavam a ferramenta. Em 2026, 45%. Ano passado, 52% responderam que a IA aumentava a produtividade. Agora, 64%. Em Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, uma empresa farmacêutica está fazendo um raio X da produção inteira.

“A gente está mapeando todos os processos que existem na companhia - são mais de 3 mil processos -, e identificar onde a IA pode ser extremamente eficiente, implementando gradualmente a inteligência artificial nesses processos, com o objetivo de que ela reduza os erros”, conta Alexandre França, presidente da Mediquimíca.

Empresas brasileiras que adotaram IA enfrentam desafio de encontrar profissionais preparados para usar a tecnologia, diz estudo — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A pesquisa também perguntou se as empresas estão enfrentando algum obstáculo para implementar a IA. Metade das empresas disse que não tem obstáculo nenhum. Resultado melhor que em 2025. Mas um número considerável disse que existe sim um problema: a falta de qualificação. De cada 100 empresas pesquisadas, 25 disseram que está faltando gente especializada para trabalhar com IA.

“A qualificação da mão de obra acaba sendo uma barreira. Das empresas que estão utilizando, uma das principais medidas que elas têm tomado é de qualificação da própria mão de obra dentro da empresa, os próprios funcionários, para que ela consiga utilizar cada vez mais a inteligência artificial”, afirma Rodolpho Tobler, economista FGV Ibre.

A empresa que monitora com IA os poços do pré-sal sabe que, nesse mercado, gente bem capacitada é tipo petróleo - recurso valioso e difícil de encontrar.

“Na nossa experiência, é muito difícil encontrar um profissional que atenda todos os requisitos que a gente precisa procurando no mercado. Formar eles dentro de casa é uma solução que a gente encontrou e atendeu muito bem esse desafio”, diz João Vitor Bernardino.

articles.title: Musk é trilionário de novo: fortuna chega a US$ 1,04 trilhão após disparada da SpaceX | G1
articles.standfirst: Ações da empresa de foguetes acumulam alta de 16,07% em uma semana e fizeram o patrimônio do empresário saltar de US$ 976,9 bilhões para US$ 1,04 trilhão, segundo a Fortune.
articles.summary: Ações da empresa de foguetes acumulam alta de 16,07% em uma semana e fizeram o patrimônio do empresário saltar de US$ 976,9 bilhões para US$ 1,04 trilhão, segundo a Fortune.
articles.body:
Elon Musk , CEO da Tesla e da SpaceX e proprietário do X, anteriormente conhecido como Twitter, discursa durante o evento de lançamento do America.gov, um novo site governamental com inteligência artificial, organizado pelo National Design Studio, no Mellon Auditorium em Washington, DC, EUA, em 29 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Kylie Cooper

Elon Musk voltou a ser trilionário após uma forte alta nas ações da SpaceX . Às 17h desta terça-feira (6), os papéis da empresa subiam 1,23%. Na última semana, porém, a alta acumulada era de 16,07%.

Com a valorização, a fortuna estimada de Musk passou de US$ 976,9 bilhões (R$ 4,86 trilhões) para US$ 1,04 trilhão (R$ 5,17 trilhões) , segundo a Fortune. O empresário, de 55 anos, é novamente a pessoa mais rica do mundo , com uma vantagem de centenas de bilhões de dólares sobre o segundo colocado.

A alta da SpaceX acelerou na segunda-feira (5), quando as ações subiram quase 8%. Musk possui cerca de 4,76 bilhões de ações da empresa, além de outras 1,3 bilhão de ações restritas que ainda não foram liberadas para ele.

Analistas do Morgan Stanley chegaram a classificar as ações da SpaceX como "baratas" considerando os preços daquele dia.

Entre os fatores citados estão o potencial de futuros produtos de inteligência artificial (IA), os avanços no desenvolvimento da nave Starship e novos contratos da empresa para serviços de computação em nuvem voltados à IA.

Musk já havia superado US$ 1 trilhão em junho

Esta não é a primeira vez que Musk ultrapassa a marca de US$ 1 trilhão em patrimônio. Ele atingiu o valor pela primeira vez em junho, quando a SpaceX abriu seu capital e suas ações dispararam. Na ocasião, Musk se tornou a primeira pessoa da história a superar US$ 1 trilhão em riqueza.

A marca, porém, durou pouco . As ações da SpaceX caíram e, duas semanas depois, o patrimônio de Musk voltou a ficar abaixo de US$ 1 trilhão. Entre 16 e 24 de junho, sua fortuna caiu de US$ 1,32 trilhão (R$ 6,57 trilhões) para US$ 957 bilhões (R$ 4,76 trilhões), segundo o Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

A queda continuou nos meses seguintes, e a fortuna chegou a US$ 683,6 bilhões (R$ 3,4 trilhões) no início de agosto. Desde então, voltou a subir com a valorização de seus negócios.

Além da SpaceX, Musk possui cerca de US$ 156,6 bilhões (R$ 779,8 bilhões) em patrimônio relacionado à Tesla , sua fabricante de carros elétricos. Ele também tem cerca de US$ 13,1 bilhões (R$ 65,3 bilhões) na Boring Company , empresa de infraestrutura, e US$ 3,42 bilhões (R$ 17 bilhões) na Neuralink .

Musk poderia dar dinheiro a todos e ainda seria o mais rico

A diferença entre Musk e os demais bilionários é tão grande que, mesmo se distribuísse parte de sua fortuna para todas as pessoas do mundo, ele ainda permaneceria no topo da lista dos mais ricos.

Há aproximadamente 8,3 bilhões de pessoas no planeta. Se Musk desse US$ 89,40 (R$ 445,2) para cada uma delas, ainda ficaria com um patrimônio de cerca de US$ 298 bilhões (R$ 1,48 trilhão) — aproximadamente US$ 1 bilhão (R$ 4,98 bilhões) a mais que Larry Page, cofundador do Google e a segunda pessoa mais rica do mundo.

Com esse valor, Musk poderia dar a cada pessoa do planeta um par de AirPods, um jantar de três pratos ou uma boa calça jeans da Levi's e ainda manteria centenas de bilhões de dólares, estimou a Fortune.

Fortunas dos bilionários oscilam com as ações

A rápida mudança na fortuna de Musk acompanha a valorização e a queda das ações de suas empresas. O mesmo aconteceu com outros dos empresários mais ricos do mundo.

Durante um breve período no ano passado, Larry Ellison, cofundador da Oracle , ultrapassou Musk e se tornou a pessoa mais rica do mundo.

O empresário de 82 anos, que possui 40% da Oracle, teve um aumento de US$ 101 bilhões (R$ 502,98 bilhões) em sua fortuna em apenas uma noite, depois que a empresa divulgou resultados que fizeram suas ações dispararem 36%.

Entretanto, dois dias depois, a fortuna estimada de Ellison havia caído US$ 34 bilhões (R$ 169,32 bilhões). No mesmo período, Musk ganhou US$ 35 bilhões (R$ 174,3 bilhões) e voltou ao primeiro lugar.

Michael Dell , que possui 40% de sua empresa de tecnologia, ganhou cerca de US$ 122 bilhões (R$ 607,56 bilhões) entre setembro de 2025 e setembro de 2026, quase dobrando sua riqueza em um ano.

No mesmo período, o patrimônio de Larry Page aumentou US$ 16,3 bilhões (R$ 81,17 bilhões), enquanto a fortuna de Jeff Bezos cresceu US$ 24,5 bilhões (R$ 122,01 bilhões).

articles.title: Compra da Warner Bros. pela Paramount cria gigante com 200 milhões de assinantes; veja os números | G1
articles.standfirst: Acordo foi concluído nesta terça-feira (6) e cria a Skydance, que será dona de franquias como 'Harry Potter', 'Game of Thrones' e 'Batman'.
articles.summary: Acordo foi concluído nesta terça-feira (6) e cria a Skydance, que será dona de franquias como 'Harry Potter', 'Game of Thrones' e 'Batman'.
articles.body:
Foto ilustrativa mostra logotipos da Paramount e da Warner Bros — Foto: Reuters

Com o anúncio da Paramount Skydance nesta terça-feira (6) sobre a conclusão da compra da Warner Bros. Discovery , as empresas formarão uma gigante capaz de alcançar 200 milhões de assinantes.

A fusão criará a empresa Skydance, que será dona de marcas como Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures, HBO, CNN, CBS, além dos serviços de streaming Paramount+ e HBO Max. No catálogo, há franquias como "Harry Potter" e "Game of Thrones", "Batman", "Missão: Impossível" e "Top Gun".

O grupo será comandado por David Ellison, filho do bilionário Larry Ellison, cofundador da Oracle – os dois já controlam a Paramount Skydance. Ynon Kreiz, ex-CEO da Mattel, será co-CEO e responsável pelas operações da nova empresa.

O acordo avaliado em US$ 110 bilhões encerra uma das maiores disputas recentes pelo controle de ativos em Hollywood. A venda da Warner Bros. era negociada desde 2025 e envolveu a concorrência de empresas como a Netflix, que chegou a oferecer US$ 83 bilhões.

A criação da Skydance tem o potencial de redesenhar o mercado do entretenimento e do streaming em todo o mundo. O g1 preparou um infográfico que compara o tamanho das empresas e mostra como a operação pode alterar o equilíbrio de forças no setor.

Veja os números da junção entre Warner e Paramount — Foto: Arte/g1

Em dezembro de 2025, a Netflix anunciou um acordo de US$ 83 bilhões para comprar parte dos ativos da Warner Bros. Discovery , com foco nos negócios de estúdio e streaming, sendo US$ 72 bilhões para acionistas e o restante para o pagamento de dívidas.

Depois, a Paramount Skydance entrou na negociação com uma proposta concorrente para adquirir a empresa inteira, incluindo os canais tradicionais.

Em fevereiro de 2026, a Warner informou que a Paramount tinha aumentado a proposta para os US$ 110 bilhões , voltados a acionistas e dívidas, e se comprometido a pagar uma multa de US$ 2,8 bilhões pela desistência do acordo com a Netflix.

A Netflix teria quatro dias para apresentar uma contraproposta , mas decidiu abandonar a disputa por considerar que, com a oferta da Paramount, "o acordo deixou de ser financeiramente atraente".

O impacto da operação vai além do valor bilionário. A Warner Bros. Discovery detém algumas das marcas mais valiosas da indústria do entretenimento, enquanto a Paramount busca ganhar escala para competir com gigantes como Netflix e Disney.

💰 A compra pela Paramount envolve todo o grupo Warner Bros. Discovery , enquanto a oferta da Netflix excluía ativos como CNN e Discovery.

🗞️ Com a conclusão do acordo, a família Ellison, aliada do presidente americano Donald Trump, passa a controlar algumas das principais marcas do jornalismo nos EUA , como a CBS News, o programa 60 Minutes e a CNN.

📺 A Paramount também ampliará sua base de assinantes e fortalecerá sua presença em cinema, TV e plataformas digitais .

articles.title: Empresas abrem programa de estágio com vagas para Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições para atuar nas empresas Braskem e Aldak seguem até o fim de outubro. Vagas são para áreas como tecnologia, engenharia, negócios e pessoas.
articles.summary: Inscrições para atuar nas empresas Braskem e Aldak seguem até o fim de outubro. Vagas são para áreas como tecnologia, engenharia, negócios e pessoas.
articles.body:
Empresas abrem programa de estágio com vagas para Salvador e Camaçari; oportunidades chegam a R$ 2.800 de salário — Foto: Bitenka / Divulgação

As empresas Braskem e a Aldak estão com inscrições abertas para programas de estágio com oportunidades para estudantes de níveis técnico e superior na Bahia e em outros estados do país. Juntas, as empresas oferecem 136 vagas para atuação em áreas como tecnologia, engenharia, negócios, pessoas, ciências e biotecnologia. As inscrições abertas até o dia 25 de outubro, na Aldak e 30 de outubro, na Braskem .

A Braskem, empresa global do setor petroquímico e de plásticos oferece 120 vagas para estudantes universitários na Bahia. Os interessados podem se candidatar até o dia 30 de outubro por meio do site do programa . As atividades têm início previsto para março de 2027.

As oportunidades são destinadas a estudantes com previsão de conclusão da graduação entre junho de 2028 e dezembro de 2029. As vagas contemplam áreas como Engenharia, Tecnologia e Dados, Ciências e Biotecnologia, Negócios e setores corporativos.

No Nordeste, são 27 vagas distribuídas entre Camaçari e Salvador , na Bahia, além de Maceió e Marechal Deodoro , em Alagoas.

Os selecionados receberão bolsa-auxílio entre R$ 2.200 e R$ 2.800 , além de benefícios como plano de saúde, seguro de vida, vale-transporte e vale-refeição para vagas administrativas, ou transporte fretado e refeitório para quem atuar nas plantas industriais. (Confira as vagas detalhadas abaixo)

Entre os cursos mais procurados pela companhia estão as engenharias Química, Civil, Elétrica e de Produção, Ciência da Computação, Ciência de Dados, Química, Biotecnologia, Administração, Economia, Ciências Contábeis, Direito, Psicologia, Marketing e Publicidade.

Segundo Cristiane Andrade, diretora de Pessoas da Braskem, o programa busca atrair novos talentos para a formação de futuros profissionais da indústria. "Ao abrir mais um ciclo do nosso Programa de Estágio, seguimos criando oportunidades para que novos talentos desenvolvam seus conhecimentos, tragam diferentes perspectivas e contribuam para os desafios reais do negócio", afirmou.

Realizado anualmente, o Programa de Estágio é uma das principais portas de entrada para carreira na Braskem. No ciclo de 2026, a seleção recebeu mais de 11 mil inscrições.

Especializada em conectvidade e comunicação para operações de alta complexidade, a Aldak está com 16 vagas abertas para seu programa de estágio 2027. As oportunidades são para estudantes de nível técnico e superior em Salvador e São Paulo (SP). As inscrições para o processo seletivo podem ser feitas página do programa .

As candidaturas de nível superior são para atuação nas áreas de tecnologia, engenharia, negócios e pessoas. Para o nível técnico, há vagas para recebimento interno e assistência técnica em Salvador e programação de rádio e montagem de sistemas em São Paulo.

Para os selecionados, a jornada de trabalho é de seis horas por dia. Eles também terão benefícios como auxílio-refeição flexível, auxílio-transporte para deslocamento em transporte público, acesso ao TotalPass e um dia de folga no mês do aniversário. Os requisitos de formação variam de acordo com cada oportunidade. (Confira as vagas detalhadas abaixo)

De acordo com Felipe Pereira, CEO da Aldak, os estagiários participarão de projetos da companhia com suporte especializado e de uma trilha de desenvolvimento técnico e pessoal. "Queremos oferecer uma formação sólida, com acompanhamento próximo e espaço para que cada participante desenvolva competências, compreenda o negócio e enxergue possibilidades de evolução", afirma.

Após a confirmação da inscrição no site , os candidatos passarão por uma primeira etapa remota, pelo WhatsApp. Nela, os participantes deverão responder por áudio a perguntas previamente definidas. Segundo a empresa, o formato permite que os estudantes participem pelo celular, sem precisar agendar um horário para o primeiro contato.

Na sequência, os candidatos farão uma avaliação com a equipe de Recrutamento e Seleção da empresa, seguida de uma imersão presencial. Aqueles que forem aprovados para as vagas iniciam suas funções no mês de janeiro, em 2027.

articles.title: Após fim de prazo para saques de recursos nas bets, contas de apostadores ainda têm R$ 1,32 bilhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Valores serão enviados a bancos, que, entre os dias 9 e 14, deverão devolver quantias a apostadores. Caixa Econômica Federal vai intermediar a devolução nos casos em que houver algum impedimento.
articles.summary: Valores serão enviados a bancos, que, entre os dias 9 e 14, deverão devolver quantias a apostadores. Caixa Econômica Federal vai intermediar a devolução nos casos em que houver algum impedimento.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Fazenda informou nesta terça-feira (6) que as contas de 26,5 milhões de apostadores nas bets ainda reúnem R$ 1,32 bilhão. O prazo para saque dos recursos das plataformas de apostas se encerrou nesta segunda-feira (5).

A proibição das bets foi anunciada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva em 25 de setembro . A vedação inclui também jogos online e cassinos virtuais no país, como por exemplo, o "Jogo do Tigrinho".

🔎Lula também enviou ao Congresso um projeto de lei que estabelece penas para quem explorar, operar ou divulgar as bets e os cassinos virtuais. Ao tomar as medidas, o petista mencionou o endividamento de famílias e o vício de apostadores em jogos de azar.

➡️ A partir desta terça-feira (6), os sites e aplicativos das plataformas de apostas estão indisponíveis. Segundo o governo, quem tentar acessar as plataformas será redirecionado para uma página com orientações sobre o resgate dos valores e as garantias de devolução dos recursos.

"De ontem para hoje, houve uma diminuição de cerca de R$ 5 milhões nos recursos, passando para R$ 1,325 bilhão na terça-feira (6). Um dos aspectos que podem estar relacionados ao ritmo de retirada dos recursos é a quantidade de contas com valores reduzidos. Ao todo, 86,2 milhões de contas possuem saldos entre R$ 0,01 e R$ 0,99, que, somados, representam R$ 15,5 milhões", informou o Ministério da Fazenda.

Com o fim do prazo de saque, as empresas terão até quarta-feira (7) para encaminhar às instituições financeiras os saldos remanescentes de cada apostador, discriminados por CPF, além da conta bancária utilizada para os depósitos.

Entre sexta-feira (9) e a próxima quarta-feira (14), as instituições financeiras deverão realizar a devolução dos valores aos apostadores.

A partir de 14 de outubro, a Caixa Econômica Federal passará a intermediar a devolução nos casos em que houver algum impedimento.

Quase 700 bets ilegais foram criadas depois da proibição anunciada pelo governo, aponta levantamento — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

De acordo com o Ministério da Fazenda, governo federal já adotou providências para derrubar mais de 11 mil sites ilegais de apostas online em uma semana de vigência da medida provisória do presidente Lula derrubou as bets no país.

Ao todo, foram derrubados 11.056 sites nesse período, sendo 1.600 somente nesta terça-feira (6), quando os sites e aplicativos das plataformas de apostas passaram a ficar indisponíveis.

Antes da publicação da MP, outros 78 mil sites ilegais já haviam sido derrubados pela Anatel a pedido do Executivo.

articles.title: Amazon Prime Day promises big discounts. But are you really saving money?
articles.summary: Prime Day is a major global shopping event — but are the savings worth it? Here's how much you really save on Prime Day.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

One of the biggest online shopping events of the year — Prime Big Deal Days — is taking place Oct. 6–7, 2026. What began in 2015 as a celebration of Amazon's anniversary has since grown into a multiday retail extravaganza that rivals Black Friday and Cyber Monday in both hype and sales volume.

But amid the excitement, an important question remains: Do you really save money during Prime Day events? Here's what you need to know before loading up your virtual cart.

Prime Day is a global sales event created by Amazon that allows Prime members to access exclusive discounts and deals on a wide range of products across the site, including electronics, home goods, appliances, beauty, clothing, and everyday essentials.

Millions participate each year: In 2026, Amazon Prime Day totaled a record $26.4 billion in U.S. online retail spending, according to Adobe . And it expects the 2026 Big Deal Days to drive another $9.9 billion in spending.

Keep in mind that to access these deals, you must be a Prime member, which costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year if you pay annually. However, Amazon offers a free 30-day trial, allowing new users to shop the event without paying up front.

When is Amazon Prime Day and Prime Big Deal Days?

Amazon held its main Prime Day event June 23–26 in 2026; its fall counterpart, Prime Big Deal Days, runs October 6–7, 2026. According to Amazon, shoppers will find discounts of 55% or more, with most products reaching their lowest prices of the year.

How much do you really save on Prime Day?

You may be wondering whether Prime Day is just another overblown shopping holiday like Black Friday , when retailers offer increasingly unimpressive deals to encourage unnecessary spending.

There's no denying that some Prime Day deals offer value; some products genuinely reach unusually low prices during these events. For this year's October sale, Amazon says more than 1 million items will be offered at their lowest Amazon price of the year so far.

Of course, that doesn't necessarily mean these deals are the lowest prices available from other retailers.

The key to taking advantage of Prime Day is having a smart shopping strategy in place to purchase items you actually need at a steep discount — not impulsively spending to take advantage of perceived savings.

Historically, shoppers have seen discounts of 30%-60% on items such as Apple AirPods, laptops, robot vacuums, smart home devices, and branded kitchen appliances. Amazon's own products, including Kindles, Fire TVs, and Echo Dots, usually come with the deepest discounts.

So yes, if you've had your eye on a specific product and it happens to be on sale during Prime Day, you could walk away with serious savings.

Keep in mind that not all the deals offered on Prime Day are really worth it. It's important to have a plan and do your research ahead of time so you know whether you're looking at a true discount.

One common tactic retailers use to encourage spending is "price anchoring," where the listed original price is inflated, making the discount look more impressive than it actually is. In some cases, the so-called sale price is just a return to the item's normal price after a brief increase in the weeks leading up to Prime Day.

Another issue is the impulse-buy nature of the event. Flash deals and lightning sales are designed to create urgency, leading many shoppers to make purchases they wouldn't otherwise consider. If you buy something you don't need — or wouldn't have bought without the flashy red countdown clock — you're not really saving money, even if the price is lower.

If you're hoping to cash in on Amazon Prime savings, it's important to make a game plan.

It's easy to get distracted by discounts and make impulsive purchases while browsing. Before you start shopping, make a list of the key items you really want. Prioritize finding deals on those must-haves — and only buy them if it makes sense for your budget.

Decide how much money you can comfortably afford to spend on Prime Day ahead of time and stick to that limit. You'll avoid throwing your budget off track and ending up with buyer's remorse.

Amazon offers personalized deals driven by AI and Alexa to help shoppers find discounts on products they're most likely to be interested in. Look for personalized suggestions within the "Recommended deals for you," "Top deals for you," and "Customers' Most-Loved" features to zero in on the deals you may be looking for.

Amazon's Subscribe and Save feature offers year-round discounts on items you need to stock up on regularly. On Prime Day, these items may have an additional discount that could help you score extra savings.

Many major retailers such as Walmart, Target, and Best Buy will have their own sales and promotions around Prime Day when they know shoppers are in the mood to splurge. Before you check out, compare the price of items in your cart across a few different retailers to ensure you're getting the lowest price overall.

articles.title: S&P 500 closes at record high as Nvidia nears $6 trillion milestone
articles.summary: Gains by the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were overwhelmingly powered by gains in tech companies.
articles.body:
The S&P 500 hit a record Tuesday as it rose for a fourth straight day, supported by rising technology stocks, hopes for a positive earnings season and a pause in oil's recent surge.

The broad-based index closed higher by 0.58%, its first record closing high since Aug. 13. The Nasdaq Composite also jumped 0.45%. It also hit a record high for the second time this week.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq's gains were overwhelmingly powered by gains in tech companies, such as chipmakers Marvell and Broadcom.

Nvidia, the world's largest public company, also rose and moved closer to becoming the first company to ever reach $6 trillion in market value. Other trillion-dollar tech stocks also rose Tuesday. Microsoft, Amazon, SpaceX, Meta Platforms and Tesla shares all traded in the green.

Investors are also looking forward to the start of the third quarter's earnings season, which begins in earnest next week with the country's biggest banks reporting their results.

"Heading into the start of the earnings season, analysts and companies have been more optimistic than normal in their earnings outlooks for the third quarter," said FactSet senior earnings analyst John Butters.

Artificial intelligence stocks are set to be a major contributor.

"At the stock level, AI infrastructure stocks are expected to drive more than half of S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3," analysts at Goldman Sachs said Friday. They forecast that Nvidia and chipmaker Micron would most likely be responsible for a third of the entire S&P 500's earnings growth this quarter.

Stocks got off to a strong start Tuesday thanks to a drop in oil prices. However, by the end of the trading day, energy prices were about flat. That did little to deter the rally in stocks, though.

Brent oil futures ended the day up 0.2%, at $100.58 per barrel, but that came after an earlier drop of as much as 3.3%. U.S. crude oil ended the day up just 1 cent, at $89.44 per barrel. Earlier, it was down more than 2.8%.

Oil's session was muted after Bloomberg News reported that Saudi Arabia's key cross-country pipeline was operating normally, after "multiple attacks" took the critical pipeline out of commission in early September. Saudi Aramco has not responded to multiple requests for comment.

The pipeline has been used as a Strait of Hormuz workaround, given that shipping traffic there remains at just a fraction of pre-Iran war levels.

Still, "the market remains nervous about potential supply disruptions from the region," ING commodities analysts overnight said. "This nervousness is likely to persist until there are signs of progress in a deal between the US and Iran. In the meantime, the risk of further escalation remains very real."

articles.title: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon sharpens warning about a corporate credit squeeze: 'The market will ask for more'
articles.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon sharpened his warning about the risks of a global bond sell-off on Tuesday, saying the world's massive competition for capital...
articles.body:
JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) CEO Jamie Dimon sharpened his warning about the risks of a global bond sell-off on Tuesday, saying the world's massive competition for capital could begin squeezing corporate borrowers.

Dimon warned that the combination of rising government borrowing costs and spending on the AI boom could spill into corporate credit markets, pushing up the costs for companies to refinance or raise new debt.

"There will be a point where the market will ask for more and more and more, and yeah, at one point that'll feed into corporate debt, corporate credit spreads, and things like that, which is how it normally happens," Dimon said in a Bloomberg interview on the sidelines of a JPMorgan event in London.

"The best thing to do with any of these things is deal with it before it becomes a crisis. If it becomes a crisis, we will deal with it. It just will be in a much less pleasant way," he added.

The warning comes as a global rout in bonds has pushed longer-term borrowing costs sharply higher in recent weeks, with the benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield recently surpassing heights not seen since 2002.

That sell-off follows the start of the war in Iran, which has driven inflation materially higher . The US economy's strength, amid those price pressures, along with the AI boom's enormous new demand for capital, has exacerbated the dynamic.

Credit markets have already begun to show signs of stress as interest rates have moved higher. In recent weeks, the spread for insuring US junk bonds has widened significantly in the credit default swap market, according to LSEG data compiled by Yardeni Research.

Last week, JPMorgan strategists flagged leveraged loans in deeply distressed territory or those trading below 60 cents on the dollar, rose to $65 billion from a year ago to their highest level since March 2020.

Dimon has been delivering versions of this argument for months. In JPMorgan's April shareholder letter, he warned that the combination of spending on AI, defense, and infrastructure, along with large government deficits, should keep upward pressure on borrowing costs.

Weeks ago, he told Yahoo Finance , shortly after the Federal Reserve's September rate hike, that while he believed borrowing costs could continue to rise, the labor market's relative strength signaled that those costs hadn't yet translated into broader economic stress.

On Tuesday, Dimon focused on how those risks could play out for companies.

articles.title: As AI bubble fears circulate, remember the railroad bust of 1873
articles.summary: While the pundits love comparing what we are witnessing with Big Tech stocks to the lead-up to the dot-com crash in the early 2000s, don't overlook how this...
articles.body:
AI stock bubble talk is percolating again as Nvidia ( NVDA ), AMD ( AMD ), and Micron ( MU ) push to record highs .

While the pundits love comparing what we are witnessing with Big Tech stocks to the lead-up to the dot-com crash in the early 2000s, don't overlook how this moment is also creeping up on the railroad bust in the late 1800s.

As the chart below from Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett shows, peak concentration for most asset bubbles in history has been capped around the 40% level, except for during the railroad boom.

The railroad bust of 1873 was a massive financial collapse driven by speculation in railroad construction. This ultimately led to the Panic of 1873.

PBS noted that 89 of the country's 364 railroads went bankrupt during the bust. A total of 18,000 businesses failed in only two years. By 1876, unemployment had risen to 14%.

No one is saying this moment with AI forward stocks is similar, but it warrants watching as valuations continue to climb on leading names — and their influence over the broader market increases.

Indeed, the stock market is pretty much being kept afloat by three tech stocks .

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) has never been more concentrated in just three stocks than it is today, with Nvidia, Apple ( AAPL ), and Microsoft ( MSFT ) representing over 21% of the index, per data from Creative Planning.

The importance of these three stocks to the S&P 500 has never been greater. Only IBM ( IBM ), AT&T ( T ), and ExxonMobil ( XOM ) could hold a candle to the three tech stalwarts of today: In the mid-1980s, those three industrial giants at their peak made up 13.4% of the S&P 500.

articles.title: Paramount closes $110 billion deal with Warner Brothers Discovery: The new company is called Skydance
articles.summary: The entity Skydance will be led by tech scion David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz, formerly the top executive at Mattel. Paramount's purchase of Warner Bros.
articles.body: The entity Skydance will be led by tech scion David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz, formerly the top executive at Mattel.Paramount's purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, which Hollywood spent most of 2026 treating as either inevitable or illegal, depending on who was paying for the lunch, is done. The parent company will be called Skydance, and David Ellison will run it alongside his incoming co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. Ellison simply reused the name of Skydance Media, his original film production company, as the umbrella for everything being folded into the new conglomerate. Paramount and Warner Bros. themselves survive as brands under that umbrella, keeping their logos on their films, much as Universal sits under Comcast.The road here was not short. Paramount offered $31 a share in cash, valuing Warner's equity at $81 billion and the whole transaction at $110 billion once debt is counted. Netflix had got there first, with a $27.75-a-share agreement for the studio and streaming assets, but when the price rose its co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters told Warner the deal was no longer financially attractive and walked away. Then came a lawsuit from twelve states. On September 30, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín approved Paramount's settlement with them, and the price of that settlement is worth reading closely. The combined company must release at least 30 theatrical films a year for two years and 32 for the following three, pay a $30 million penalty for every film it falls short, and honour 45-day theatrical windows. It must also set up an independent editorial board to oversee CNN and CBS News. Rarely has a merger been approved on the condition that it behave like two companies.Which brings us to Kreiz, the most interesting hire in Hollywood this year. At Mattel since 2018, he turned toy brands into films, TV shows and games, and delivered "Barbie," the highest-grossing film Warner Bros. has ever had. The man who rented Warner its biggest hit now gets the keys to the building. He will oversee daily operations and the combined businesses, while Ellison leads strategy, creative and technology. Ellison, in short, keeps the vision and hands Kreiz the spreadsheet.That spreadsheet is not a gentle one. Paramount is aiming for more than $6 billion in savings from the merger, and Kreiz's turnaround at Mattel included job cuts. To fund the purchase, Paramount is issuing about $42.4 billion in bonds and taking out a further $8.5 billion and €850 million in loans. Three Middle Eastern funds will own 38.5% of the merged company, according to Paramount. The leadership reshuffle has already begun: Warner Bros. Pictures chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy will not be part of Ellison's team.Ellison describes Skydance as "a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling." The settlement, with its film quotas and per-title fines, suggests that twelve state attorneys general were not entirely prepared to take his word for it.(With wire inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: The world has nearly burned through its oil stockpile buffer, executives say
articles.summary: By Robert Harvey, Stephanie Kelly and Shadia Nasralla LONDON, Oct 6 (Reuters) - The amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market is runni...
articles.body:
By Robert Harvey, Stephanie Kelly and Shadia Nasralla

LONDON, Oct 6 (Reuters) - The amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market is running low, industry executives said at a forum in London this ‌week, making the market more fragile and putting upward pressure on prices.

Governments and energy companies have drawn oil from ‌stockpiles to alleviate pressure in a global oil market facing unprecedented supply disruptions this year due to the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.

"Less than ​6 billion barrels of commercial inventories remain today, with the vast majority not practically available, so the system is already straining," Amin Nasser, CEO of Saudi Arabia's state oil company Saudi Aramco, said at the Energy Intelligence Forum in London.

More than 1 billion barrels of oil have been released mainly from onshore commercial inventories since the start of this year's Middle East crisis, which was the last major tool in ‌the box, Nasser said.

The International Energy Agency, the ⁠West's oil watchdog and coordinator of its strategic oil reserves, is preparing to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel to help alleviate soaring diesel prices, but it is not clear if ⁠some of that total will include volumes from its record first 400 million barrel release in March that hadn't hit the market yet.

"It took a lot of negotiations, but it is 100 million," Nasser said of the IEA decision. "Inventories are reaching a stress level. Only 10% or ​less is ​available, that's why they struggle with 100 million barrels."

World oil demand ​is about 102 million barrels per day, according to ‌the IEA.

SUPPLY RESILIENCE CUSHION IS SCARILY THIN

The loss of the oil market's buffers has made the market more fragile, Chevron CEO Mike Wirth said on Tuesday, adding that this has increased oil's price floor.

Oil market turmoil will continue beyond next year, executives said at the conference on Monday, as it could take years to refill inventories on top of meeting global demand.

Not all oil in storage is immediately usable because of operational factors like tank bottoms or oil sat in pipelines, as well as political factors like government ‌rules dictating minimum levels of emergency stocks.

There is huge demand to build ​additional inventories around the globe, Nasser added. Kuwait Petroleum Corporation CEO Shaikh ​Nawaf Al-Sabah said his company is aiming to build out ​storage domestically and at its overseas refineries.

The world is reliant on the seaborne oil exports escaping the ‌Middle East "to keep things in balance as we go ​through winter, because there aren't ​any more inventories to drain in the West," the CEO of commodities trader Vitol Russell Hardy said.
authors: By Robert Harvey, Stephanie Kelly and Shadia Nasralla

articles.title: Why corporate boards no longer view CEO security as just a perk
articles.summary: Security is now considered a requirement for top executives, according to the Conference Board.
articles.body:
Protecting a CEO is no longer a gift the board gives to top executives, along with a country club membership and access to a private plane. These days, top-flight security has become a requirement, according to Conference Board CEO Steve Odland.

"It is a real issue. You know, a few years ago, you would have security under the title of a perk," Odland said on Yahoo Finance's Sozzi Unleashed . "They are no longer perks when CEOs are getting shot in the back. It is a requirement in order to do the job."

Fresh data from the Conference Board underscores the trend:

34% of S&P 500 CEOs now report having personal and home security, up from 18% in 2024.

11% of Russell 3000 CEOs report having security, up from 5% in 2024.

Among Russell 3000 companies with at least $50 billion in annual revenue, 60% of CEOs now receive personal and home security benefits.

The pickup in spending reflects the unfortunate new reality.

In December 2024, UnitedHealthcare ( UNH ) CEO Brian Thompson was fatally shot outside a Manhattan hotel in a targeted attack prior to the company's annual investor conference.

The suspect, Luigi Mangione, was apprehended days later at a McDonald's in Pennsylvania carrying a 3D-printed ghost gun, a silencer, and a handwritten manifesto expressing hostility toward the US healthcare industry.

The high-profile assassination sent shockwaves through corporate executive security teams and boards.

"When you have your children threatened, you need security," Odland said. "You need to be taken care of. You can't walk through airports. And these aren't perks. This is part of protecting your assets of the firm. And more boards are stepping up to say, 'OK, we realize that we've got to do this.' And so it gets imputed in pay."

articles.title: Deeply Distressed US Loans Rise to Highest Level Since Pandemic, JPMorgan Says
articles.summary: The deeply distressed tail of the leveraged loan universe has grown to levels not seen since the beginning of the pandemic, with technology the single bigges...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The deeply distressed tail of the leveraged loan universe has grown to levels not seen since the beginning of the pandemic, with technology the single biggest sector under pressure.

That's according to strategists at JPMorgan Chase & Co., who on Tuesday wrote that the value of loans trading below 60 cents on the dollar, or deeply distressed levels, rose to $65 billion from $40 billion a year ago, to the highest since March 2020.

Distressed leveraged loans, or those trading at or below 80 cents on the dollar, are also on the rise, totaling $139.8 billion, a nearly 90% jump over the past 12 months and just $4 billion shy of a high in May 2020, strategists including Nelson Jantzen wrote in a report.

There are now about 141 leveraged loan issuers trading below 80 cents on the dollar, 35 more than a year earlier, with names including software providers CDK Global, QLIK Technologies Inc., and Quest Software among the biggest contributors.

The biggest concentration of distressed loans is in the technology sector at 39%, with a total of $54.4 billion, according to the report.

Software companies are facing an increasingly challenging refinancing environment as a wall of more than $100 billion of maturing debt is approaching. The sector came under pressure this year with concerns mounting that advances in artificial intelligence would disrupt businesses offering software services.

In the riskiest part of the leveraged loan market, returns on CCC loans, the lowest tier of junk, are down 1.97% year-to-date, compared with gains in every other junk-rated category, according to JPMorgan.

On the high-yield bond side of distress, spreads on debt rated CCC have jumped above 1,000 basis points, the highest since the 2023 regional banking crisis when investors dumped risky debt. Yields on CCC bonds have climbed to 15.58%, the highest since November 2022.

CCC spreads have been rising steadily in recent months as soaring global bond yields and the Federal Reserve's pivot to tighter policy added to pressure on highly levered borrowers by boosting debt service and refinancing costs just as a large chunk of bonds and loans comes due.

The JPMorgan strategists noted that the high-yield bond volume affected by defaults year-to-date is outpacing that of loans, "the first time this has occurred since 2020." The bank expects both high-yield bond and leveraged loan default rates to rise next year from a projected 2.25% in 2026 to 2.75% and 4.50% respectively.

articles.title: Lush expands India presence, plans 30 stores in five years
articles.summary: Lush to expand in India with 30 stores in five years, up from its 10-year plan; aims for 8 stores by FY27 and grows Bengaluru local production.
articles.body: BENGALURU: To Rowena Bird, India looks very different from the market Lush first entered years ago. The 1995-founded British cosmetics brand, whose founders created the bath bomb, had arrived before premium beauty had really taken off here. Malls were fewer. Imported brands were less familiar. Even Lush’s unpackaged soaps and fizzing bath bombs often needed explaining.This time, Bird believes the market is ready.“The market has very much changed,” the Lush co-founder told TOI. “There are a lot more Western brands... people are open to looking at something new.”Bird said Lush’s mistake the first time was entering too early. Import taxes were high and the market for premium cosmetics was still developing. “I don’t think the market was really ready for us,” she said.The shift is encouraging Lush to move faster in India. Its original business plan envisaged 30 stores over 10 years. It projected annual sales of around £11 million at that scale. The India team now believes it could reach the store target in about five years.Lush currently has five stores in the country. It expects to have eight in FY27 and is forecasting India sales of just under £2 million for the year. Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Hyderabad are next on its expansion map. Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru are expected to eventually have multiple stores.“We are already, in terms of number of stores, doing more than our plan,” said Vishal Anand, who leads Lush’s India business. “I think we should be able to achieve that plan in five years.”Bird said India is currently performing slightly better than Lush had projected. Even at the planned 30-store scale, however, the country would be a medium-sized market for the company. Lush operates across about 55 markets.Local manufacturing is also increasing. Lush currently makes six products at its Bengaluru “fresh kitchen”. These already account for about 6% of India sales. The company plans to increase the locally made range to 30 products, largely across fresh face packs, hair masks, eye pads and cleansers.The Bengaluru unit has enough capacity to support as many as 50 stores. But Lush does not expect to manufacture its entire portfolio in India. Much of the wider assortment will continue to be imported.Indian customers have also challenged some of Lush’s early assumptions. Shower products account for about 26% of sales and haircare about 23%. Bath bombs, which the company thought could be a harder sell in India, have also performed better than expected.Customers typically buy more than two products per transaction, the company said. articles.title: Hershey adds new disclaimer on wrapper after Reese's pumpkin lawsuit
articles.summary: The newly printed disclaimer, located underneath the image of the jack-o-lantern face in the chocolate, reads, "Carving not on actual product."
articles.body:
Hershey has added a new disclaimer to its Reese's Peanut Butter Pumpkins following a lawsuit against the candy company for deceptive marketing.

As of Oct. 6, Reese's Peanut Butter Pumpkins have a new disclaimer printed on the front of the packaging that reads, "Carving not on actual product." The disclaimer is situated underneath a rendering of the pumpkin-shaped candy that shows a mouth and eyes carved into the chocolate, resembling a jack-o-lantern.

Reese's Peanut Butter holiday candies previously had a disclaimer that read, "Decorating Suggestion," but USA TODAY confirmed the new messaging on this season's packaging. Hershey has not shared why the disclaimer was adjusted. USA TODAY reached out to the company on Oct. 6 for more information.

Customers may have noticed the change after Florida District Judge Melissa Damian on Sept. 16 dismissed a case filed in May 2024, accusing Hershey of deceptive marketing for several Reese's Peanut Butter products, including Reese's Peanut Butter Pumpkins, according to court documents. This is the second time Damian has dismissed the case, the first of which was in September 2025.

Damian wrote in her most recent filing that the only injury the plaintiffs experienced was "their subjective disappointment," as outlined in court documents.

What was the lawsuit over Reese's Peanut Butter Pumpkins?

In May 2024, Florida residents Nathan Vidal, Debra Kennick, Abdjul Martin and Eduardo Granados sued Hershey, alleging the company engaged in "unlawful, fraudulent, unfair, misleading and/or deceptive" advertising of several candies, according to court documents.

In 2023, Vidal purchased three bags of Reese's Peanut Butter Pumpkins because he "believed that the product contained a cool-looking carving of a pumpkin's mouth and eyes," according to court documents. But when he opened the chocolates, he found them to be blank.

Vidal said he would not have purchased the chocolates if he knew they didn't feature the details as pictured on the packaging.

In addition to Reese's pumpkins, the plaintiffs addressed concerns with peanut butter ghosts, bats, footballs and winter shapes, like snowmen, stockings and bells.

The group demanded $5 million from Hershey, which they claimed represented the sale of Reese's Peanut Butter products in Florida since 2021.

Hershey argued reasonable consumers would understand the images on the packaging as suggestions and pointed to a "Decorating Suggestion" disclaimer on the packaging. The company also argued customers received exactly what they paid for: Reese's candies that were not defective or inedible.

articles.title: AT&T settlement approved. Here's how much customers get
articles.summary: AT&T's $177 million data breach settlement won final approval. Here's how much eligible customers could receive.
articles.body:
A federal judge has granted final approval to AT&T's $177 million settlement resolving lawsuits over two 2024 data breaches that exposed personal information belonging to millions of customers.

U.S. District Judge Sidney Fitzwater in Dallas approved the settlement Oct. 2, along with $59 million in attorneys' fees for lawyers who negotiated the deal, according to Reuters. The settlement faced dozens of objections, including arguments that the amount was inadequate compared to a $350 million settlement in separate litigation involving T-Mobile.

For AT&T customers who filed valid claims, the amount they receive depends on which data breach affected them, what information was exposed and whether they can document financial losses. Most customers receiving the tiered cash payments are expected to get far less than the settlement's advertised maximums.

Customers could receive between about $6.50 and $40 through the tiered payment system, according to court documents . Here's what to know.

The settlement has two funds totaling $177 million: $149 million for customers affected by the first data incident, known as AT&T 1, and $28 million for customers affected by the second incident, known as AT&T 2.

Customers in the AT&T 1 settlement class could receive either a documented-loss payment of up to $5,000 or a tiered cash payment. Customers in the AT&T 2 class could receive a documented-loss payment of up to $2,500 or, for eligible customers, a Tier 3 payment.

Tier 1: $39 to $40. This is for AT&T 1 customers whose Social Security numbers were exposed.

Tier 2: $7.50 to $8.10. This is for AT&T 1 customers whose information was exposed but whose Social Security numbers were not.

Tier 3: $6.50 to $7.10. This is for eligible AT&T 2 customers whose information was exposed in the second data incident.

The amounts are estimates, not guaranteed payments. Tiered payments are calculated on a pro rata basis from the remaining settlement funds after documented-loss payments and other approved expenses are paid.

Customers seeking compensation for documented losses had to provide evidence that the losses were "fairly traceable" to a data incident. The settlement website says qualifying losses could include certain expenses related to fraud or identity theft, while some losses, including medical bills, emotional distress and estimated lost wages, were not eligible.

Nearly 5 million claim forms had been submitted as of Aug. 24, 2026, according to the court's final approval order. The settlement administrator had received 754,263 paper claims and 4,163,810 electronic claims, for a total of 4,918,073 claims.

A 66-year-old recently retired engineer wants to give each of his three adult children $19,000 a year from the couple's $1.5 million portfolio. He wants to see them enjoy the money now rather than wait for an inheritance.

His wife, 64, disagrees. She thinks the kids should earn it like they did and worries that $57,000 a year in gifts could put their own retirement at risk.

The tax rules make those gifts relatively straightforward. The harder question is whether the couple can afford them.

Want rental property income without fixing leaky faucets or screening tenants? Arrived lets you invest in rental homes starting at just $100

There's More Than One Way To Put Cash To Work. Some Accredited Investors Are Looking Beyond Savings Accounts.

What The IRS Gift Rules Actually Allow In 2026

The IRS allows each person to give up to $19,000 per recipient in 2026 without counting that amount against the donor's lifetime gift and estate tax exemption.

That means the husband could give each of his three children $19,000, or $57,000 total, without using his lifetime exemption, assuming the gifts qualify for the annual exclusion.

His wife has her own $19,000 annual exclusion for each child. Married couples can also elect to split gifts , allowing up to $38,000 per child to qualify for the annual exclusions, although gift splitting generally requires both spouses to consent and file a gift tax return.

Federal estate tax isn't a pressing concern for a couple with $1.5 million. The basic exclusion amount for 2026 is $15 million per person .

The real question isn't whether the IRS will tax these annual gifts. It's whether the couple can afford to make them year after year.

Why $57,000 A Year Changes The Retirement Math

Giving $57,000 a year equals 3.8% of their $1.5 million portfolio.

If they also need $60,000 a year for their own living expenses, their planned portfolio withdrawals would total $117,000, or 7.8% of the starting portfolio.

That doesn't automatically mean the plan will fail. Investment returns, Social Security, spending needs, taxes and longevity all matter.

But a retiree taking substantial withdrawals from a portfolio has less room to absorb poor market returns, particularly early in retirement. That's the core of the wife's concern.

A financial plan should therefore test the couple's retirement spending and the proposed gifts together rather than treating the $57,000 as money that's automatically available.

articles.title: America has a new favorite convenience store
articles.summary: The winning convenience store is better known as a Midwest grocery chain - than quick-stop gas station
articles.body:
America has a new favorite convenience store – and no, it's not Buc-ee's , according to new data.

In fact, the Texas -based beaver-themed chain with a massive fanbase has fallen behind several competitors in this year's customer satisfaction rankings. Buc-ee's earned a score of 77 out of 100 in the American Customer Satisfaction Index's 2026 Convenience Store Study, tying for 4th place alongside Maverik, Pilot, RaceTrac, and Shell.

So, which chain took the top spot? It was Meijer.

The Midwest retailer, better known for its sprawling grocery stores than its convenience stores, jumped five points to 82, earning the highest customer satisfaction score among the more than two dozen convenience store brands evaluated by the index.

Meijer operates about 500 stores across Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Wisconsin and Kentucky, with around 230 Meijer Express locations offering gas, coffee, grab-and-go food and everyday essentials.

QuikTrip, Sheetz and Wawa tied for 2nd place, each scoring 80.

Kwik Trip, which topped last year's rankings with a score of 84, fell six points to 79 and tied for 3rd place with Murphy USA.

Buc-ee's tied for 4th place with Maverik, Pilot, RaceTrac and Shell, with each chain scoring 77.

The rankings are based on 9,475 customer surveys collected between October 2025 and September 2026. The index evaluated convenience stores on factors including food quality, cleanliness and store layout, merchandise variety, employee courtesy, checkout speed, store hours and coffee quality.

Overall satisfaction with convenience stores slipped 1 percent this year to a score of 75. Customers gave lower marks to mobile apps, store cleanliness and employee interactions. Mobile order pickup, which was measured for the first time this year, received a score of 82.

Buc-ee's still performed well in the South, where Wawa took the top spot with a score of 82, just one point ahead of Buc-ee's. Sheetz led the Midwest with an 83, while Wawa also topped the Northeast. Maverik and QuikTrip tied for first in the West.

The results mark a notable shift for Buc-ee's, which has built a cult following around its enormous stores, extensive food selection and famously clean restrooms. But the chain has also faced backlash in recent months over the aggressive enforcement of its cartoon beaver trademark.

In July, Buc-ee's sued Beaver's Mini Mart in Beavercreek, Ohio, alleging the convenience store's cartoon beaver logo was too similar to its own mascot.

Last month, Buc-ee's also settled a separate lawsuit with Mickey's, an Ohio gas station chain, after accusing its cartoon moose mascot, Mickey, of infringing on Buc-ee's trademark. Mickey's had countersued, arguing that customers could easily tell the difference between a moose and a beaver.

articles.title: Novavax, Moderna stocks fall after WHO calls plague risk 'low'

articles.body:
Novavax stock ( NVAX ) fell on Tuesday after a World Health Organization (WHO) spokesperson told reporters that there was a "low" risk of a plague epidemic, after a 28-year-old woman who worked in a Russian anti-plague laboratory died last week .

Shares of Novavax fell nearly 10%, pulling back from a 20% gain the day before that was fueled by concerns about a potential outbreak. Moderna ( MRNA ) stock fell 7%, giving back all its gains from Monday. BioNTech ( BNTX ) fell 2%, while Pfizer ( PFE ) was little changed.

A worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East died of "pneumonia of undetermined" origin last week, raising concerns about a potential global health scare.

The WHO is investigating whether the death was due to pneumonic plague, a highly contagious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Pneumonic plague is curable with antibiotics if caught early, but it can be fatal within 24 hours of onset if left untreated, WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said.

Lindmeier noted that Shipilova's workplace was "an institute that studies dangerous pathogens, including plague, in a part of Siberia where plague occurs naturally in wild animals."

Lindemeier said WHO had identified and tested the worker's contacts and did not detect plague or pathogens of dangerous infectious diseases.

"None to date have shown symptoms of illness," he said of the contacts.

WHO "estimates the risk to be moderate to low for Irkutsk, a low risk for the Russian Federation as a whole and very low for the WHO European region," Lindmeier added.

US officials have called on Russia to be more transparent about the incident. Russian authorities reportedly put one hospital facility and dozens ‌of people under quarantine.

"I think it's incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more ‌information with the ⁠world," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday. "We're watching it very closely, hour by ⁠hour."

articles.title: Man deposits Rs 85.3 lakh received as cash gifts from wife, relatives; income tax calls it unexplained and sends notice, but ITAT Chennai accepts gift deeds and gives relief
articles.summary: You get a lot of gifts in the form of cash and you deposit the amount in your bank account.
articles.body: You get a lot of gifts in the form of cash and you deposit the amount in your bank account. But, what if the Income Tax Department treats them as unexplained income and sends you a notice.In one such case in Chennai, a man received cash gifts of Rs 85.03 lakh from his relatives. After learning of this the Income Tax Department sent notices to the man and his relatives. The man eventually won relief in ITAT Chennai.What the case is aboutIn this case the man who received the cash gifts formalised the transactions through gift deeds and deposited the money into his bank account. He had received money from his wife, paternal uncles, maternal uncle and sister’s husband, all of whom fall within the definition of “relative” under Income Tax law.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or saleUnder Income Tax law, banks are required to report specified financial transactions (SFT) when customers deposit or withdraw large amounts of cash. In this case, the bank reported the transaction involving the Rs 85.03 lakh cash deposit to the Income Tax Department.After receiving the information, the Income Tax Department began making enquiries into the source of the Rs 85.03 lakh deposited by the man. The department also sent tax notices to the relatives who had given him the cash. The donors responded to the notices and confirmed the gifts. According to their responses, the gifts had been made between April and September 2016.The man also submitted documents to substantiate his claim. These included copies of the gift deeds, acknowledgements of the donors’ income tax returns, their income statements and financial statements.However, the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) in Chennai questioned whether the donors had sufficient financial capacity to give such substantial amounts in cash. According to the AO, the income disclosed by the relatives in their ITRs and the capital reflected in their balance sheets did not correspond with the value of the gifts they had made to the man.The Income Tax Department therefore treated the cash deposited in the bank account as unexplained and passed an order holding that the amount represented a violation of Income Tax law.The man challenged the addition before the Commissioner of Appeals (CIT A), but the CIT (A) was also not persuaded by his explanation. The appellate authority upheld the addition of Rs 85.3 lakh in respect of the gifts received and passed its order on December 29, 2025.The man eventually succeeded before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Chennai on September 18, 2026.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claimWhy did the man win cash gifts case in ITAT?The key question before ITAT Chennai was whether the Rs 85.3 lakh in cash gifts received by the man could actually be treated as unexplained cash credits under Section 68, as the Income Tax Department had concluded.ITAT Chennai said that, in its considered opinion, the man had discharged the initial burden placed on him under Section 68 once he furnished confirmations from the donors, gift deeds, copies of their income tax returns (ITRs) and financial statements. The donors had also personally acknowledged having made the gifts in response to notices issued under Section 133(6).The tribunal observed that if the AO still had doubts about the actual source of funds available with the respective donors, it was for the Income Tax Department to conduct the necessary enquiry while assessing those donors, according to an ET report.ITAT Chennai said: “The addition in the hands of the recipient cannot be sustained merely because the AO entertains suspicion regarding the source available with the donors, particularly when the identity of the donors and the genuineness of the transactions have not been disputed.”ITAT Chennai noted that the established legal position is that, unless a particular provision of law specifically requires otherwise, an assessee generally cannot be required to prove the source of funds in the hands of a creditor once the creditor’s identity, the genuineness of the transaction and basic creditworthiness have been established.The tribunal made a similar observation in relation to the other donors. It found that the authorities had essentially compared the income disclosed by the relatives in their ITRs with the amounts they had gifted, without examining their overall financial position, including accumulated capital, withdrawals, cash balances and other resources available to them.Also Read | Man paid Rs 1.73 crore for Gurgaon flat, waited over a decade without possession; builder alleges homebuyer bought it for commercial gain, consumer commission awards refund with 12% interest & Rs 4 lakhITAT Chennai said: “Suspicion, however strong, cannot take the place of legal evidence.”The tribunal further noted that the donors themselves had disclosed the gifts in their respective financial statements and that the Income Tax Department had not controverted this fact.ITAT Chennai also observed that the Income Tax Department had failed to place any material on record to show that the cash deposited into the bank account had, in fact, originated from him.Sarthak Prashar, Director, Global People Solutions at Grant Thornton Bharat, told ET that the man succeeded before ITAT Chennai because he produced adequate evidence to establish the identity of the relatives who had given him the cash gifts. The documents also supported the genuineness of the gift transactions.Prashar says gifts received from certain specified relatives are not taxable even when their value is more than Rs 50,000. Section 92(5) (g) sets out the specified relatives, which include parents, grandparents, spouse, brother, sister and others.However, the ITAT Chennai case highlights the difference between the tax treatment of a gift and the need to substantiate the transaction. A gift may be exempt from tax because it comes from a specified relative, but the tax authorities can still examine whether the transaction is genuine and whether it is backed by appropriate evidence.Prashar says receiving a gift from a relative that is exempt from tax does not, by itself, mean that the recipient must file an income-tax return. Whether an ITR needs to be filed depends on the recipient’s total income and the other provisions governing return filing.Also Read | Man sells ancestral agricultural land for Rs 8 crore, buys two properties and claims LTCG exemption; faces Rs 6.36 crore tax additions, why ITAT Chandigarh gave relief under Sections 54B and 54FYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: CNN, CBS News now under one roof as Paramount-Warner Bros merger closes
articles.summary: The newly combined company is called Skydance and began trading on Wall Street on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Paramount Skydance has completed its $110bn merger with Warner Bros Discovery to form Skydance.

The deal, which closed on Tuesday, brings together two entertainment giants that own movie studios and theme parks, but also brings two of the United States’ most influential news brands under one roof — CNN and CBS News.

Skydance CEO David Ellison, son of tech tycoon Larry Ellison, who is also a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has appointed Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. Kreiz previously led Mattel.

The road to the merger has included lawsuits from unions and 12 different state attorneys general . But the deal was ultimately settled after the company agreed to appoint an independent editorial board to oversee both news networks amid concerns that the merger would lead to skewed coverage at the two networks.

On Monday, the company announced that Mark Thompson will stay on as CNN’s editor-in-chief, while Bari Weiss, editor-in-chief at CBS News, who was appointed to the role a year ago on Monday , will stay in her position.

Thompson’s continuation brought “ a sigh of relief ” among journalists at CNN, its media industry newsletter, Reliable Sources, reported.

Ever since the merger had been announced, there had been a wave of concerns at the network that major changes would be made to CNN if the Ellisons took over.

There are still a lot of unknowns about what news will look like under Skydance. In a memo to staffers on Monday, Thompson said that “the specifics of how CNN will plug into and operate in the new company have yet to be finalized.”

That means looming fears of layoffs and consolidation still weigh on both news divisions as the combined company will carry $80bn in debt, while the entertainment giants look to cut costs, grow their streaming footprint and have pledged to produce 30 movies per year .

Thompson’s stay may be temporary, as The New York Times reported that his contract is up in the spring.

It is also not yet clear whether the networks will stay separate or combine in the long term, amid concerns that CBS News’ Weiss could be handed additional charge of CNN. In the past, the network’s top talent, including journalist Anderson Cooper, has threatened to leave if she came on board.

Weiss took over the network one year ago, and viewership has slumped across the board. Most recently, the news magazine programme 60 Minutes saw viewership slump during its season premiere last month, dropping 21 percent from the prior year and marking its worst viewership for a season premiere in 25 years, according to Nielsen ratings.

The terms of the attorneys general’s lawsuit settlement require an independent editorial oversight board for both the networks. Skydance has 180 days to put it together. Press freedom experts do not believe that will help maintain editorial independence.

“It doesn’t take effect for 180 days. The newsroom can be totally overhauled in 180 days,” Seth Stern, director of advocacy for the Freedom of the Press Foundation, told Al Jazeera.

It is not the first time a publication has appointed an editorial board to weigh in on concerns about editorial influence. In 2007, when News Corp acquired Dow Jones, the parent company of the Wall Street Journal, the Bancroft family, which owned the publisher at the time, was concerned that new owner and media mogul Rupert Murdoch would impact the paper’s editorial independence with his conservative tilt.

The paper appointed a five-person independent committee to preserve editorial integrity. But it was later revealed, including by former members of the board during a roundtable discussion hosted by the Freedom of the Press Foundation, that it did not deliver the oversight that it was originally intended to provide.

In Skydance’s case, the board is to be made up of five journalists appointed by Ellison, and there is no requirement for the company to disclose its findings to the public. The terms say that no more than two people on the board can be affiliated with the same political party.

“The truth isn’t dictated by the fifty-yard line between political parties. Sometimes neither political party is even close to the truth. So having a commitment to bipartisan representation, as opposed to a commitment to truth-telling, totally misunderstands what news is,” Stern said.

On Wall Street, the new company began trading under the ticker symbol SKYD. Since opening on Tuesday, the stock has dropped 2.5 percent.

How rising mortgage rates are hitting the housing market hard

Rising mortgage rates are lowering the odds of prospective homebuyers entering the market and adding to the tough economic slate for President Trump and the GOP ahead of the midterms.

The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate was 7.28 percent last week, the highest mark since late November 2023, according to data from Freddie Mac. The average rate also rose by a quarter point from the week prior, the largest week-to-week increase in four-plus years.

Rising mortgage rates are part of a rough financial ledger for Trump and Republicans, as inflation remains above 3 percent and fuel prices stay elevated amid the Iran war.

“Economy, cost of living, that kind of congealing will be [important], certainly it has been for the last … two years, for voters in ‘26,” GOP strategist Matt Gorman told The Hill.

Experts point to multiple factors for why mortgage rates have shot up above 7 percent. Lawrence Yun , the chief economist at the National Association of Realtors (NAR), noted increased energy prices during the Iran conflict have pushed inflation up.

Annual inflation, as measured by the personal consumption expenditures price index, has increased from 2.8 percent in February to 3.4 percent in August , according to data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis.

articles.title: ‘A Skydance Corp.’: David Ellison immediately puts his stamp on Warner Bros.
articles.summary: The deal blends two historic film studios, two streaming platforms and two news organizations.
articles.body: LOS ANGELES — On Tuesday, as some employees at Warner Bros. logged on to their laptops, they were met by a logo that signaled a changing of the guard. SKYDANCE, written in all caps, underlined. Similar branding was also quietly added below the famous Warner Bros. water tower in Burbank, California, where the studio’s storied lot is located, and at the company’s New York City office. The message was clear for all to see: The $110 billion Paramount-Warner merger of two Hollywood giants closed Tuesday, and CEO David Ellison isn’t taking any time to dwell on the past. “We’re proud to write this next chapter with you,” Ellison and newly tapped co-CEO Ynon Kreiz wrote in a roughly 1,000-word memo to employees, which was titled “Day 1,” a copy of which was shared with NBC News. “Now the real work begins. Let’s go!” Ellison’s emphasis on rebranding and moving forward signals an effort to put his own stamp on Hollywood at a moment of significant industry change. But that push will likely come with consequences that could affect the industry as a whole, with some worried what greater corporate control could mean for the future of entertainment and media. The merger blends two historic film studios (Paramount and Warner Bros.), two popular streaming platforms (Paramount+ and HBO Max) and two news organizations (CBS News and CNN) under the leadership of the 43-year-old Ellison, son of Oracle chief Larry Ellison, who is a close ally of President Donald Trump. Larry Ellison is personally backing the deal with tens of billions of dollars of his own fortune. David Ellison’s nearly yearlong journey to close the deal had its ups and downs. Many outspoken actors, writers and producers in Hollywood rallied behind efforts to block the merger, arguing in an open letter earlier this year that further corporate consolidation of the entertainment industry will “threaten the sustainability of the entire creative community.” After the deal was approved by the U.S. Justice Department, the European Commission and dozens of other countries worldwide, it was held back by a lawsuit led by California’s Democratic attorney general, Rob Bonta. Bonta and other state attorneys general argued that the deal, if completed, would reduce competition and potentially imperil the journalistic independence of CNN. But what once looked like a formidable legal challenge folded quickly. Paramount Skydance, led by Ellison, reached a deal with the states on Sept. 21, which requires the combined company to release 30 films per year for the first two years of the deal, followed by 32 films in each of the following three years — or pay a fee for missing that target. Ellison also pledged to establish independent editorial boards overseeing the operations of CNN and CBS News. J. Christopher Hamilton, a Syracuse University professor and an entertainment attorney, said that the merger’s completion is “a bittersweet victory, depending on which side of the table you sit on.” “There’s reason to celebrate and be excited, but also there’s a sobering reality when layoffs start to hit people unexpectedly,” he said. “And there’s fewer and fewer outlets for character-driven pieces and art-house pieces, true independent film voices getting a chance to be heard.” Ellison and Kreiz described the merger and rebrand as “the beginning of a new era in entertainment.” “This isn’t a merger of convenience,” they wrote in their memo. “It’s the beginning of a new era in entertainment, and we wanted a name that looks forward rather than one that simply splices together the past.” But the two hinted that layoffs are likely, writing that “integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce. We are committed to handling this process thoughtfully and respectfully.” Already, there has been some restructuring and shake-ups at the executive level. Ellison enlisted Kreiz, who is known for cutting costs at Mattel, where he served as CEO and helped turn Barbie from a doll into a Hollywood blockbuster. HBO’s Casey Bloys will be the leader of the company’s combined streaming efforts, with Paramount streaming chief Cindy Holland announcing her departure last week. Mike de Luca and Pam Abdy, Warner’s film chiefs, also exited, and Ellison appointed Paramount Pictures co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein to lead the expanded film division. On the news side, Mark Thompson is staying on at CNN as chairman ⁠and editor in chief of ​CNN Worldwide. Bari Weiss will continue to lead CBS News as editor in chief. Skydance said in a news release Tuesday that Ellison will “chair the Skydance Board of Directors, and continue to serve as Skydance’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer.” The board will also add Kreiz, media mogul Laurene Powell Jobs and Bobby Kotick, founder and former CEO of Activision. Hamilton, who has worked at Hollywood companies including Lionsgate and Viacom, said leadership shuffles are par for the course. “I don’t have any doubts that the Ellisons are going to make a lot of noise when it comes to shaking up Hollywood, leading these legacy media companies as this new conglomerate,” the entertainment attorney said. However, he added, “I question the sincerity and consistency when pressure mounts and it’s contrary to what they want to do, whether it’s AI regulations or expectations from the labor unions, whether it’s storytelling and having a true reflection of diverse voices. When pressure shows up, are they really going to be fair? Or are they going to be like, ‘No, this is my ball, I control the game.’” It’s a concern that opponents of the merger have had since it was first floated as a possibility. Critics have warned the deal will lead to layoffs, fewer opportunities and higher prices. On Monday, a group of private named individuals filed an emergency request for the Supreme Court to get involved in the merger, claiming that the terms of the states’ deal “do not preserve competition between Paramount and Warner Bros.” The Supreme Court denied the request for the court to get involved. Actor Mark Ruffalo, one of the staunchest members of the Block the Merger movement, vowed to continue pushing back against media consolidation. “This was never about just one merger: this was about fighting back against corrupt oligarch billionaires trampling the interests of everyday people to line their own pockets,” Ruffalo wrote in a post on X last week. “We’re still in that fight.” Skydance’s stock price had dropped 2.5% by Tuesday afternoon, closing at $9.53 per share. Trump told reporters he was “happy” about the deal formally closing, saying it’s a “great merger.”
